Bilhaṇa
Son of Jyeṣṭhakalaśa an. Nāgadevī an. grandson of Rājakalaśa of Kashmir; middle of 11th Cent.; left home in about 1062-65 A. D. an. went to different courts before he composed his historical poem Vikramāṅkadevacarita in C. 1085 A. D. in the court of Cālukya Vikramāditya VI of Kalyan; ment. by Kalhaṇa in Rājataraṅgiṇī VII. 938; by Maṅkha in Śrīkaṇṭhacarita, Report CXII; q. by Gadādhara in Rasikajīvana, BORI. D. XII. 247; in Sp. an. Sbhv. an. other anthologies; by Bhoja in Śṛṅgāraprakāśa. See V. Raghavan Bhoja's Śṛṅgāraprakāśa p. 857.
On Bilhaṇa an. his works see B. N. Misra, Studies on Bilhaṇa an. his Vikramāṅkadevacarita. [Page008-b]
--Karṇasundarī. nāṭikā.

Bilhaṇa(kavi)
ins. poet. favourite an. trusted Prime minister of King Vindhyavarmadeva (1160-1180) of Dhara of Paramāras of Malwa; also a resident of Dhara; praises Āśādhara; composed the inscription of Maṇḍu (a hymn to God Viṣṇu) of Vindhyavarmadeva.
C.. biracitamiha biSNodami vAkyaprasUnaizcaraNasatatapUjA bAkkRtA bilhaNena … viMdhyavarmanRpateH prasAdabhUH sAMghivigrahikabilhaNakaviH etc. ed. by K. K. Lele, Dhar, ABORI. XI. 49ff. [Page008-a.

Bilhaṇacarita
incorporating the Caurapañcāśikā traditionally ascribed to Bilhaṇa; said to have been composed to record a secret intrigue with a princess Candralekhā, daughter of Vīrasim3ha of Mahilapattana according to Kashmir version an. Yāminīpūrṇatilakā, daughter of Madanābhirāma of Pāñcāla according to Southern version. [Page009-a.
According to Bengal tradition she is Vidyā, daughter of King Vīrasim3ha an. the poet-hero is Sundara (also called Corakavi).
See Keith, HSL. p.. 188-89. Dasgupta, HSL. I. p. 368.
